records.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. One finished clinical illustration panel for an airline-safety-card style recovery guide. Primary request: a two-state sequence in one panel about removing a head dressing after ear surgery. LEFT: one calm adult seen in profile, wearing a snug wrapped white elastic bandage band (not a towel) that wraps over the crown and covers the area behind one ear, both hands gently lifting the band upward off the head. CENTER: one bold teal arrow pointing right. RIGHT: the same adult in profile with the dressing fully removed being set aside, and one connected circular detail inset magnifying the area behind the ear where a small strip of white medical tape sits on healthy skin. Style/medium: precise late-20th-century airline safety-card illustration (image only, absolutely no lettering); controlled navy linework, flat color fills, sparse print-like stipple, believable adult human anatomy with complete coherent hands, utilitarian and instructional rather than cute, painterly, or photorealistic. Color palette: UCSF-derived navy, teal, pale blue, warm neutral skin tones, small yellow accents; off-white background. Constraints: ZERO typography anywhere — no words, no title, no caption, no letters, no numerals, no labels of any kind; the top 12 percent and bottom 15 percent of the panel stay completely empty off-white for later UI overlays; no stray marks or floating shapes; no mascot characters; no incision, wound, blood, stitches, or internal anatomy visible at any point; no device brands; generous whitespace at the edges for UI overlays; landscape 4:3 single panel.
